_what_this_is: A third image set, written to CHOOSE a cut for the image path rather than to describe the model.
_why_they_exist: src/README.md line 25 ends at the same sentence: choosing a cut for image-bearing messages needs a set written for that purpose, and none had been. On the first 32 cases the accuracy-maximal cut is the interval (0.134, 0.168], pinned by exactly one case on each side (i6 and a8), so the boundary rested on two pictures that were never chosen to be boundary cases.
source: hand-written in this project's own session (seek-opensource-task), 2026-10-25, after calibration/vision/probe.json was produced
question: Do you need to do something about this message? Answer act or ignore.

labels.act: the picture shows something this bot must act on
labels.ignore: the picture shows nothing this bot must act on

design_note: Every case is assigned to a content family before anything is scored, and the label follows the picture: the act half carries THIN evidence (one amber tile among twelve, one ERROR line among INFO, a gauge at 91%, an SLO just crossed, a warn counter trending up) and the ignore half carries EVIDENCE-LIKE pictures that are benign (a red brand header over an all-green status page, an incident marked RESOLVED, an audit reporting zero errors, a dip annotated recovered, a red announcement slide, a backup that COMPLETED). Cases were never dropped or kept for their score: all 24 are reported whatever they scored. Captions stay uninformative, as in the other two sets. Three act labels are disputable on reflection (b-a1 one amber tile, b-a4 and b-a10 a certificate 21 and 18 days out) and the reading is also computed without them.
